messages:
alex_m: Heads up — eu-west1 started failing GPU attaches ~19:02 UTC. Logs show a lot of scratchpool reclaim activity and high nvme latency.

maria_ops: saw the same. Pod create waits >30s then times out. Heap of small files being deleted by janitor. IOPS to local nvme pegged.

pranav_infra: dmesg snippet from one host:
```
[ 1234.567890] nvme0n1: I/O 4321 QID 0 timeout, status: 0x9
[ 1234.568002] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 987654
[ 1234.569101] zone_reclaim: page allocation stalls, kworker backlog
```

alex_m: interesting bit: the janitor starts aggressive delete/rename after OOM -> reclaim scans many tiny files -> lots of small random reads/writes -> async fsync pileup. That kills the local SSD queue depth.

infra-bot: ALERT: scratchpool-scrub backlog > 85% on eu-west1 (09 hosts) :exclamation:

maria_ops: mitigation ideas: 1) throttle janitor scans (lower concurrency / increase backoff) 2) temporarily route new GPU allocs to us-west2 3) add ephemeral-ssd buffer nodes to soak deletes

sam_sre: we can also toggle `reclaim.batch_size` to 16 from 256 to reduce IOPS. But that increases reclaim window and SSD wear still accumulates. Cost tradeoff: extra nodes vs longer reclaim period.

pranav_infra: quick patch deployed to reduce janitor concurrency to 8 (was 64). Also pushed a kernel parameter bump for `nvme_max_submissions` on the fleet as 2-min canary.

alex_m: thanks. early numbers: iops dropped 60%, attach success rate went from 58%->92% in affected region. But one host hit a readonly remount during the spike, kernel logs show scrub job triggered EIO.

maria_ops: opened a short maintenance window for eu-west1 to drain 15 risky nodes and reprovision with fresh ephemeral pools. ETA 40m.

sam_sre: follow-ups: 1) add guardrails in janitor to stop deletes if nvme latency >100ms 2) implement backoff that considers current `iostat` metrics 3) long-term: consider larger blocksize GC or move tiny-file hotspots to object-store-backed cache.

pranav_infra: logging note — added a `janitor.iops_ratio` metric to the console and an alert when reclaim uses >50% of local disk bandwidth.

alex_m: one more: check PMEM/firmware counters for the host that remounted readonly. If hardware failing we need reprovision and warranty RMA.

infra-bot: NOTE: incident created #INC-9543, assignees: @pranav_infra @maria_ops

maria_ops: will follow up with cost calc for buffer nodes vs extended reclaim window and record in the incident.

alex_m: good job on the rapid throttle. Keep updates in INC-9543, and if we see replay in other regions we escalate to emergency provisioning. :thumbsup:
